proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(Q=10^6\), let \(T_{xy}=Qt_8(x,y)\) be the integer matrix in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}n8\mbox{-}full\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}certificate}\), and, directly from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}hypergeometric\mbox{-}kernel}\), put
\[
 c_N(x,y):=
 \sum_{\substack{0\leq t_a\leq a,\ 0\leq t_p\leq p,\ 0\leq t_q\leq q,\ 0\leq t_b\leq b\\
 t_a+t_p+t_q+t_b=4,\ t_p+t_b=x,\ q+b-t_q-t_b=y}}
 \binom a{t_a}\binom p{t_p}\binom q{t_q}\binom b{t_b}.
\]
Because \(\binom84=70\), the kernel identity gives \(K_N(x,y)=c_N(x,y)/70\) and \(\sum_{x,y}c_N(x,y)=70\).  The largest absolute entry of \((T_{xy})\) is \(744266<Q\), so \(t_8\) is feasible.  Since \(\tau_N=(p-q)/8\), denominator clearing gives the exact identity
\[
 R_N^{\mathrm{CR}}(t_8)
 =\frac{S_N}{4480000000000000},\qquad
 S_N:=\sum_{x,y}c_N(x,y)\{8T_{xy}-Q(p-q)\}^2.
\]
Set
\[
 M:=292992750491520=640\cdot457801172643.
\]
For \(p\geq q\), define
\(
 \delta_{p,q}:=M-\max_{0\leq a\leq8-p-q}S_{(a,p,q,8-a-p-q)}.
\)
Substitution of the binomial coefficients in the preceding finite sum gives the exhaustive triangular table
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
p&(q,\delta_{p,q})\\ \hline
0&(0,0)\\
1&(0,25780350722816),\ (1,74633180406656)\\
2&(0,28487201038976),\ (1,101366778351616),\ (2,150726698175616)\\
3&(0,20276478648640),\ (1,103205642527616),\ (2,185543066360064),\ (3,237987455841920)\\
4&(0,1042769664),\ (1,96025992016704),\ (2,177021364878208),\ (3,255669909370880),\ (4,292992750491520)\\
5&(0,5610019299520),\ (1,88299771155200),\ (2,165931651853120),\ (3,236516348250240)\\
6&(0,747443840),\ (1,120018517677760),\ (2,195440555456000)\\
7&(0,38080886782080),\ (1,138035999899520)\\
8&(0,1293664640).
\end{array}
\]
This covers every pair \((p,q)\) with \(p+q\leq8\): exchanging the treatment and control labels maps \((a,p,q,b),(x,y),\tau_N\) to \((a,q,p,b),(y,x),-\tau_N\), while the displayed matrix has \(T_{yx}=-T_{xy}\).  Hence
\(
 S_{(a,p,q,b)}=S_{(a,q,p,b)}.
\)
For the sole zero in the triangular table, the nine slacks \(M-S_{(a,0,0,8-a)}\), in order \(a=0,\ldots,8\), are
\[
 (292992750491520,269063856160640,0,323070080,698375552,
 323070080,0,269063856160640,292992750491520).
\]
All other displayed slacks are positive.  Thus \(S_N\leq M\) for all
\(
 |\mathcal N_8|=\binom{11}{3}=165
\)
states, with equality only at \((2,0,0,6)\) and \((6,0,0,2)\).  Finally,
\[
 \frac{M}{4480000000000000}
 =\frac{457801172643}{7000000000000}=U_8,
\]
which proves the asserted primal upper certificate directly from the response-type kernel.

We next verify the new full-count prior lower certificate.  Let \(q_N^{\mathrm{CR}}\) be the eleven integer masses in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}n8\mbox{-}full\mbox{-}lower\mbox{-}certificate}\), so \(\pi_{8,N}^{\mathrm{CR}}=q_N^{\mathrm{CR}}/Q\).  Every displayed mass is positive, and
\[
 2(22437)+2(110421)+2(2584)+2(138475)+2(84082)+284002
 =1000000=Q.
\]
Define the integer aggregates
\[
 \alpha_{xy}^{\mathrm{CR}}:=\sum_Nq_N^{\mathrm{CR}}c_N(x,y),\qquad
 \beta_{xy}^{\mathrm{CR}}:=\sum_Nq_N^{\mathrm{CR}}c_N(x,y)(p-q),\qquad
 \gamma^{\mathrm{CR}}:=\sum_Nq_N^{\mathrm{CR}}(p-q)^2.
\]
Direct substitution in the hypergeometric sum gives \(\gamma^{\mathrm{CR}}=15253448\) and
\[
\begin{array}{c|r|r@{\qquad}c|r|r}
(x,y)&\alpha_{xy}^{\mathrm{CR}}&\beta_{xy}^{\mathrm{CR}}&(x,y)&\alpha_{xy}^{\mathrm{CR}}&\beta_{xy}^{\mathrm{CR}}\\ \hline
(0,2)&177235&-553900&(2,0)&177235&553900\\
(0,3)&3184525&-14369090&(3,0)&3184525&14369090\\
(0,4)&4893862&-29138640&(4,0)&4893862&29138640\\
(1,1)&103360&0&(2,2)&11885772&0\\
(1,2)&3630260&-4431200&(2,1)&3630260&4431200\\
(1,3)&10075852&-26544120&(3,1)&10075852&26544120\\
(1,4)&3184525&-14369090&(4,1)&3184525&14369090\\
(2,3)&3630260&-4431200&(3,2)&3630260&4431200\\
(2,4)&177235&-553900&(4,2)&177235&553900\\
(3,3)&103360&0&&&
\end{array}
\]
and all omitted cells have zero predictive mass.  The check
\(
 \sum_{x,y}\alpha_{xy}^{\mathrm{CR}}=70000000=70Q
\)
verifies total predictive mass one, and every displayed \(\alpha_{xy}^{\mathrm{CR}}\) is positive.  Since \(\tau_N=(p-q)/8\), the Bayes-dual moments are
\[
 A_{xy}^{\pi_8^{\mathrm{CR}}}=\frac{\alpha_{xy}^{\mathrm{CR}}}{70Q},\qquad
 B_{xy}^{\pi_8^{\mathrm{CR}}}=\frac{\beta_{xy}^{\mathrm{CR}}}{560Q},\qquad
 \sum_N\pi_{8,N}^{\mathrm{CR}}\tau_N^2=\frac{\gamma^{\mathrm{CR}}}{64Q}.
\]
Consequently Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}finite\mbox{-}bayes\mbox{-}dual}\) gives, by exact rational square completion,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal B_{(X_1,X_0)}(\pi_8^{\mathrm{CR}})
 &=\frac{15253448}{64\cdot10^6}
 -\sum_{(x,y):\alpha_{xy}^{\mathrm{CR}}>0}
 \frac{(\beta_{xy}^{\mathrm{CR}})^2}
 {64\cdot70\cdot10^6\alpha_{xy}^{\mathrm{CR}}}\\
 &=\frac{23126566130927189325821140923541183}
 {353617236146857430307249306610000000}=C_8.
\end{aligned}
\]
The finite minimax duality in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}response\mbox{-}type\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}games}\) therefore yields \(C_8\leq\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}\).

For completeness, independently verify the difference-only lower certificate in the same kernel.  Let \(q_N^W\) be the eleven displayed integer weights defining \(\pi_8^W\).  They are positive and
\[
 2(25164)+4(92977)+2(37394)+2(92573)+317830=1000000=Q.
\]
For \(j=x-y\), set
\[
 c_N(j):=\sum_{x-y=j}c_N(x,y),\qquad
 \alpha_j^W:=\sum_Nq_N^Wc_N(j),\qquad
 \beta_j^W:=\sum_Nq_N^Wc_N(j)(p-q),\qquad
 \gamma^W:=\sum_Nq_N^W(p-q)^2.
\]
Substitution gives \(\gamma^W=15211060\) and
\[
\begin{array}{c|r|r}
j&\alpha_j^W&\beta_j^W\\ \hline
-4&4686730&-27876820\\
-3&6696400&-29975170\\
-2&10482010&-27731530\\
-1&7413920&-9297700\\
0&11441880&0\\
1&7413920&9297700\\
2&10482010&27731530\\
3&6696400&29975170\\
4&4686730&27876820.
\end{array}
\]
Here \(\sum_j\alpha_j^W=70000000=70Q\), and every \(\alpha_j^W\) is positive.  Because \(W=2j\), the same square completion gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal B_W(\pi_8^W)
 &=\frac{15211060}{64\cdot10^6}
 -\sum_{j=-4}^4\frac{(\beta_j^W)^2}{64\cdot70\cdot10^6\alpha_j^W}\\
 &=\frac{224641744872980943629642927781}
 {3414537001722982784239360000000}=L_8.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(L_8\leq\rho_8^W\).  The remaining comparisons are certified by
\[
 \frac{6541}{100000}-U_8
 =\frac{68827357}{7000000000000}>0,
 \qquad
 \frac{6578}{100000}-\frac{6541}{100000}=\frac{37}{100000}>0,
\]
\[
 L_8-\frac{6578}{100000}
 =\frac{33500899643136082377826981}
 {3414537001722982784239360000000}>0,
\]
and
\[
 U_8-C_8
 =\frac{6035118823618189262769785976715289}
 {35361723614685743030724930661000000000000}>0.
\]
Combining the primal and dual bounds proves the complete displayed sandwich.  Since its full-count endpoints are distinct, the certificates deliberately make no assertion that either equals the unknown exact value \(\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(n\geq1\) and \(L_{\mathrm{bd}}<U_{\mathrm{bd}}\).  In the bounded finite-population ATE problem of Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}hull\mbox{-}bounded\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}risks}\), the minimax risk over all assignment designs and all measurable estimators is
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^\star[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]
 =\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2
 \min_{d\in[0,2]^{n+1}}
 \max_{\substack{k,\ell\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\\k+\ell\leq n}}
 \sum_{x=0}^n2^{-\ell}\binom{\ell}{x-k}
 \left(d_x-\frac{2k+\ell}{n}\right)^2,
\]
where \(\binom\ell r=0\) off \(r\in\{0,\ldots,\ell\}\).  It is attained under independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment.  More precisely, writing
\[
 A_i=\frac{Y_i(1)-L_{\mathrm{bd}}}{\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}},\qquad
 C_i=\frac{U_{\mathrm{bd}}-Y_i(0)}{\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}},\qquad
 Z_i^\circ=D_iA_i+(1-D_i)C_i\in[0,1],
\]
and \(p_x(z)=[u^x]\prod_{i=1}^n(1-z_i+z_i u)\), any endpoint action \(d\in[0,2]^{n+1}\) extends to the estimator
\(
 \Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}\{\sum_xd_xp_x(Z^\circ)-1\}.
\)
For this extension, the risk is separately convex in every coordinate of \((A,C)\in[0,1]^{2n}\), so its maximum over the full bounded cube is attained at a binary endpoint vertex and equals the maximum of the displayed shifted-binomial risks indexed by \((k,\ell)\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(n\geq1\) and \(L_{\mathrm{bd}}<U_{\mathrm{bd}}\).  Under independent \(D_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), Hull's affine estimator
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{AF}}
 =\frac{\sqrt n}{\sqrt n+1}\widehat\tau^*,\qquad
 \widehat\tau^*=\frac2n\sum_{i=1}^n(2D_i-1)
 \left(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\frac{U_{\mathrm{bd}}+L_{\mathrm{bd}}}{2}\right),
\]
has maximum squared-error risk over all schedules in \([L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]^{2n}\) equal to
\(
 \Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2/(\sqrt n+1)^2.
\)
Consequently \(\mathfrak R_n^\star[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]\leq\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2/(\sqrt n+1)^2\).

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(L_{\mathrm{bd}}<U_{\mathrm{bd}}\) and every \(n\in\{2,4,6,8\}\), balanced complete randomization is strictly suboptimal in Hull's class of all bounded schedules and all measurable estimators:
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^\star[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]
 <\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{bal}}[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}].
\]
For \(n\in\{2,4,6\}\), the explicit certificate is
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{bal}}[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]
 \geq\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}
 >\frac{\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2}{(\sqrt n+1)^2}
 \geq\mathfrak R_n^\star[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}].
\]
At \(n=8\), the rational certificate is
\[
 \mathfrak R_8^{\mathrm{bal}}[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]
 \geq\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2 C_8
 >\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2 I_8
 \geq\mathfrak R_8^\star[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}].
\]
The independent-design endpoint action \(d_8\) has normalized worst-case risk exactly \(I_8\), attained only at Hull states \((k,\ell)=(0,3)\) and \((5,3)\).  This theorem proves only the four displayed finite even cases; it makes no assertion for any even \(n\geq10\), and Hull's uniform-in-\(n\) strict-suboptimality conjecture remains open.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(L_{\mathrm{bd}}<U_{\mathrm{bd}}\) and abbreviate \(\Delta=\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}>0\).  We first prove the only direction in which the binary result transfers to the bounded cube.  Given any binary schedule \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))_{i=1}^n\), embed it as the endpoint schedule
\[
 y_{id}=L_{\mathrm{bd}}+\Delta Y_i(d),\qquad d\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Its bounded causal ATE is
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(y_{i1}-y_{i0})
 =\frac\Delta n\sum_{i=1}^n\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)\}
 =\Delta\tau_N.
\]
For any measurable bounded-data estimator \(\widehat\tau\), define on this endpoint subclass
\[
 \widetilde t\bigl(Z,(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_i\bigr)
 :=\Delta^{-1}\widehat\tau
 \bigl(Z,(L_{\mathrm{bd}}+\Delta Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_i\bigr).
\]
The positivity \(\Delta>0\) justifies division, and the risk identity is
\[
 \mathbb E_Z\left[\left\{\widehat\tau-Delta\tau_N\right\}^2\right]
 =\Delta^2\mathbb E_Z\left[\left\{\widetilde t-\tau_N\right\}^2\right].
\]
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}response\mbox{-}type\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}games}\) proves that the minimax risk over all labeled binary-data estimators under balanced complete randomization is \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}\).  Since the endpoint schedules form a subclass of the bounded schedules, taking first the supremum and then the infimum in the preceding identity yields
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{bal}}[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]
 \geq\Delta^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}. \tag{1}
\]
No orbit reduction is asserted for nonbinary schedules: equation \((1)\) uses the binary two-count reduction only after restricting nature to the endpoint subclass.

For \(n=2\), Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}n24\mbox{-}equality}\) gives \(\rho_2^{\mathrm{CR}}=1/4\).  Since \(\sqrt2>1\), one has \((\sqrt2+1)^2>4\), and hence
\[
 \rho_2^{\mathrm{CR}}=\frac14>\frac1{(\sqrt2+1)^2}.
\]
For \(n=4\), the same theorem gives \(\rho_4^{\mathrm{CR}}=1-\sqrt3/2\), and
\[
 1-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}>\frac19
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \sqrt3<\frac{16}{9}.
\]
The latter inequality follows by squaring the positive sides, since \(3<256/81\).

For \(n=6\), Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}n6\mbox{-}seven\mbox{-}state\mbox{-}saddle}\) gives \(\rho_6^{\mathrm{CR}}=s_6^2\) and its defining interval gives \(s_6>29/100\).  Also
\(
 \sqrt6>2449/1000
\)
because \(6>2449^2/10^6=5997601/10^6\).  Therefore
\[
 s_6(\sqrt6+1)>
 \frac{29}{100}\frac{3449}{1000}
 =\frac{100021}{100000}>1.
\]
All factors are positive, so squaring and dividing proves
\[
 \rho_6^{\mathrm{CR}}=s_6^2>\frac1{(\sqrt6+1)^2}.
\]
The cited Hull affine certificate \(\mathrm{lem{:}hull\mbox{-}independent\mbox{-}affine\mbox{-}upper}\) supplies an independent-design estimator with maximum risk \(\Delta^2/(\sqrt n+1)^2\).  Combining it with equation \((1)\) proves the displayed strict chain at \(n=2,4,6\).

It remains to certify the sharper independent bound needed at \(n=8\).  For integers \(k,\ell\geq0\) with \(k+\ell\leq8\), define the normalized endpoint risk of \(d_8\) by
\[
 H_{k,\ell}:=
 \sum_{j=0}^{\ell}2^{-\ell}\binom\ell j
 \left(d_{8,k+j}-\frac{2k+\ell}{8}\right)^2.
\]
This is exactly the shifted-binomial risk in \(\mathrm{lem{:}hull\mbox{-}bounded\mbox{-}global\mbox{-}reduction}\), because the endpoint observation is \(k+\operatorname{Binomial}(\ell,1/2)\) and the normalized target is \((2k+\ell)/8\).  Put \(D_0=2^{14}10^{12}=16384000000000000\) and
\(
 \sigma_{k,\ell}:=D_0(I_8-H_{k,\ell}).
\)
Substituting the nine integers defining \(d_8\) and clearing the common denominator gives all \(45\) slacks:
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
k&(\sigma_{k,0},\ldots,\sigma_{k,8-k})\\ \hline
0&(4577441792,3880130560,30789297309696,0,238862336,
53461707285504,105693419993088,97336380346880,3580346880)\\
1&(327965806819328,359818810488832,281843022690304,293958109724672,
358362791708672,371515404700672,283644940700672,97336380346880)\\
2&(660197382158336,530887778891776,581356140759040,631689073692672,
560408945692672,371515404700672,105693419993088)\\
3&(787093695625216,855369846626304,824582262626304,631689073692672,
358362791708672,53461707285504)\\
4&(985221165627392,855369846626304,581356140759040,293958109724672,
238862336)\\
5&(787093695625216,530887778891776,281843022690304,0)\\
6&(660197382158336,359818810488832,30789297309696)\\
7&(327965806819328,3880130560)\\
8&(4577441792).
\end{array}
\]
Every entry is nonnegative, and the only zero entries are \((k,\ell)=(0,3)\) and \((5,3)\).  Hence
\[
 \max_{k,\ell\geq0:\,k+\ell\leq8}H_{k,\ell}
 =I_8=\frac{481065022279}{8000000000000},
\]
with precisely those two maximizers.

We spell out why this endpoint calculation controls the full bounded cube.  In the normalization of \(\mathrm{lem{:}hull\mbox{-}bounded\mbox{-}global\mbox{-}reduction}\), for fixed assignment \(D\), each \(Z_i^\circ=D_iA_i+(1-D_i)C_i\) is affine separately in \(A_i\) and \(C_i\).  The Bernstein polynomial
\(
 \mathcal B_{d_8}(z)=\sum_xd_{8,x}p_x(z)
\)
is multi-affine in \(z\), while the normalized causal target \(n^{-1}\sum_i(A_i+C_i)-1\) is affine in every coordinate.  Thus, holding all other coordinates fixed, their difference is affine in either \(A_i\) or \(C_i\), its square is convex, and averaging over \(D\) preserves convexity.  Successively maximizing each coordinate over \([0,1]\) therefore moves a maximizer to a vertex of \([0,1]^{16}\).  The vertices are exactly the shifted-binomial states indexed by the \(45\) pairs \((k,\ell)\).  The independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) Bernstein-extension estimator associated with \(d_8\) consequently has maximum bounded-schedule risk exactly \(\Delta^2 I_8\).  In particular,
\[
 \mathfrak R_8^\star[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]\leq\Delta^2I_8. \tag{2}
\]

The strengthened Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}n8\mbox{-}strict\mbox{-}separation}\) and equation \((1)\) give
\(
 \mathfrak R_8^{\mathrm{bal}}\geq\Delta^2C_8.
\)
Exact subtraction yields
\[
 C_8-I_8
 =\frac{1489964546219114077997554988878251203581}
 {282893788917485944245799445288000000000000}>0.
\]
Combining this inequality with equation \((2)\) proves the claimed strict comparison at eight.  Finally, \(\mathrm{lem{:}hull\mbox{-}bounded\mbox{-}global\mbox{-}reduction}\) identifies \(\mathfrak R_n^\star\) as Hull's joint optimum over all designs and all measurable estimators.  The proof has exhausted only \(n\in\{2,4,6,8\}\); it supplies no inequality for \(n\geq10\), so the uniform conjecture is left open.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: The primary binary estimand is \(\tau_N=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)\}=(p-q)/n\). For the bounded-class corollary, a schedule \(\mathbf y=(y_{i1},y_{i0})_{i=1}^n\in[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]^{2n}\) has causal ATE \(\tau(\mathbf y)=n^{-1}\sum_i(y_{i1}-y_{i0})\); on the binary endpoint embedding \(y_{id}=L_{\mathrm{bd}}+\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}Y_i(d)\), it satisfies \(\tau(\mathbf y)=\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}\tau_N\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The directed bounded-outcome corollary uses the same causal ATE on a larger support and requires the endpoint scaling relation to be explicit.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: The primary binary fixed-design functional is \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}=\min_t\max_{N\in\mathcal N_n}\sum_{x,y}K_N(x,y)\{t(x,y)-\tau_N\}^2\). The bounded-outcome corollary compares the fixed balanced-design functional \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{bal}}[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]\) with the all-design, all-measurable-estimator functional \(\mathfrak R_n^\star[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]\) from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}hull\mbox{-}bounded\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}risks}\).

prose_updates.tldr: Exact balance removes treatment-share variation but leaves two observed arm-success counts. For fixed binary potential outcomes, the full pair and its difference have equal worst-schedule ATE squared-error minimax risk at \(n=2,4,6\), but a rational two-sided full-count bracket and a difference-only lower certificate prove strict loss at \(n=8\). The endpoint subclass also yields a separate bounded-outcome design result: balanced complete randomization is strictly worse than Hull's independent-design optimum at \(n=2,4,6,8\). Both later-even compression persistence and Hull's uniform-in-\(n\) strictness conjecture remain open.

project_justification.gap: Published minimax analyses establish the all-design shifted-binomial reduction and report numerical evidence that complete randomization remains strictly suboptimal with general estimators, but do not give exact endpoint certificates for that strict comparison. They also do not locate the first finite size at which compressing the two exact-balance success counts to their difference loses minimax information.
project_justification.niche: The fixed-half binary response-type hypergeometric experiment supplies exact primal-dual certificates, while its binary endpoint embedding supplies rigorous lower bounds for the full bounded schedule class without claiming a nonbinary two-count reduction.
project_justification.fill: The project gives analytic equality saddles at \(n=2,4,6\), rational lower and upper full-count certificates and strict count-compression separation at eight, and exact finite bounded-class comparisons showing balanced complete randomization is strictly suboptimal relative to independent assignment at \(n=2,4,6,8\).

prose_updates.related_work: Hull (2026, Theorem 1 and Appendix A.4) optimizes worst-case ATE squared error jointly over all bounded schedules, assignment designs, and measurable estimators, proves that independent half assignment attains the shifted-binomial minimax program, and uses Bernstein extension plus separate convexity to lift endpoint risks to the full bounded cube. Corollary 1 gives the affine independent-design risk \(\Delta^2/(\sqrt n+1)^2\); footnote 12 records uniform strict suboptimality of complete randomization with general estimators as a conjecture supported numerically. Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}hull\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}complete\mbox{-}randomization\mbox{-}strict\mbox{-}small\mbox{-}n}\) proves that comparison only for \(n=2,4,6,8\), leaving the uniform conjecture open. Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) study the same unrestricted independent-design scalar program and its Airy expansion, not the exact balanced hypergeometric count-compression threshold. Ding and Dasgupta (2016) supply the binary response types and observed table used in the finite kernel. Blackwell (1953) gives only weak dominance of the full count pair over its difference. Bai (2023) treats permutation-invariant linear procedures. Rigdon and Hudgens (2015), Li and Ding (2016), and Li and Ding (2017) concern exact confidence sets or first-order finite-population limits and do not imply the point-estimation or bounded-design claims here.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The two rational full-count certificates at \(n=8\) are distinct: \(C_8<\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}<U_8\) is not proved, only \(C_8\leq\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}\leq U_8\), and \(C_8<U_8\), so the exact value remains unknown. An arbitrary prior can make the second count Bayes-informative even at sizes where the minimax values agree. The bounded-class result uses only the valid endpoint-subclass lower-bound direction and does not reduce nonbinary observations to two success counts.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The theorem-level scope consists of the exact binary response-type games, equality at \(n=2,4,6\), strict count-compression separation and a two-sided full-count bracket at \(n=8\), the resulting first-lossy-size conclusion, and strict bounded-class suboptimality of balanced complete randomization at \(n=2,4,6,8\). The paper makes no confidence-set claim, pointwise-dominance claim, exact \(\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}\) claim, or two-count orbit claim for nonbinary schedules. Strict count-compression persistence for even \(n\geq10\), Hull's uniform complete-randomization conjecture, and every asymptotic rate, exponent, parity law, or constant for the balance or compression tax remain open.

statement_notes.justification: A rational action and two rational priors certify a two-sided full-count bracket and strict information value without solver tolerances or an asserted exact optimum.
statement_notes.gap: Neither Blackwell weak dominance nor Hull's all-design reduction supplies the fixed-design two-count versus difference-only separation or the exact full-count lower bracket at eight.
statement_notes.consumer: Users of \(\operatorname{complete\_ra}\) with \(n=8\) learn that retaining both arm-success counts lowers certified worst-schedule risk and that the full-count minimax value lies between \(C_8\) and \(U_8\).
